:::{#thm-invertible-cancel}
#### An invertible factor can be cancelled

Let $\matr{A}$ be an invertible $p \times p$ matrix (@def-invertible-matrix),
and let $\matr{B}$ and $\matr{C}$ be $p \times n$ matrices.
If $\matr{A}\matr{B} = \matr{A}\matr{C}$, then $\matr{B} = \matr{C}$.

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\matr{B}
&= \matr{I}_p\,\matr{B}
&& \text{(@thm-identity)}
\\
&= (\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{A})\,\matr{B}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-inverse)}
\\
&= \matr{A}^{-1}(\matr{A}\matr{B})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{A}^{-1}(\matr{A}\matr{C})
&& \text{(} \matr{A}\matr{B} = \matr{A}\matr{C} \text{)}
\\
&= (\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{A})\,\matr{C}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_p\,\matr{C}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-inverse)}
\\
&= \matr{C}.
&& \text{(@thm-identity)}
\ea
$$

$\square$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#cor-invertible-cancel-right}
#### An invertible factor can be cancelled on the right

Let $\matr{A}$ be an invertible $p \times p$ matrix,
and let $\matr{B}$ and $\matr{C}$ be $n \times p$ matrices.
If $\matr{B}\matr{A} = \matr{C}\matr{A}$, then $\matr{B} = \matr{C}$.

The proof of @thm-invertible-cancel works with every product reversed:
multiply both sides on the right by $\matr{A}^{-1}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-invertible-cancel}
#### Solving for a matrix by cancelling an invertible factor

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
which is invertible with
$\matr{A}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & -0.5 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
(@exm-invertible-matrix).
If $\matr{A}\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$
for a $2 \times 1$ matrix $\matr{B}$,
then multiplying both sides on the left by $\matr{A}^{-1}$,
as in the proof of @thm-invertible-cancel,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{B}
&= \matr{A}^{-1} \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Check:
$\matr{A} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 + 1 \\ 0 + 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

:::
